job.description:
About Supabase 

 Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

 About the role

 Supabase is scaling its AWS partnership across multiple go-to-market motions, and gaming is one of the fastest-moving. This role owns the AWS gaming segment end to end, driving adoption of Supabase within game studios building on AWS, and managing the technical and commercial relationship with AWS's gaming ecosystem (GameLift, gaming ISVs, and gaming-focused SI/SA teams).

 You'll work closely with our SI partner ecosystem (including gaming-focused system integrators) on feature enhancements, run co-sell motions with AWS gaming account teams, and build the pipeline that proves out gaming as a durable growth motion for the AWS relationship.

 What you'll do

- 
 Own the AWS gaming segment strategy and roadmap

- 
 Manage relationships with AWS's gaming team (GameLift, gaming ISV/partner org) and gaming-focused AWS SAs

- 
 Drive the SI partnership motion with gaming systems integrators -- including scoping technical gap analyses (SDK coverage across Unity, Unreal, Godot), negotiating MNDAs/agreements, and managing joint GTM plans

- 
 Build and run co-sell pipeline with AWS gaming account teams through ACE

- 
 Identify and close gaps in Supabase's gaming-specific product story (SDK support, real-time/multiplayer patterns, missing feature parity vs. incumbents)

- 
 Represent the gaming motion in AWS SCA/funding conversations, providing data and narrative to support investment asks

- 
 Partner with product marketing on gaming-specific content, case studies, and launch narratives

 Who you are

- 
 3-5+ years in partnerships, alliances, or business development, ideally with AWS or another hyperscaler

- 
 Experience working with or in the gaming industry (studios, publishers, or gaming-focused ISVs/SIs) a strong plus

- 
 Track record managing complex, multi-stakeholder partner relationships (SI partners, hyperscaler field teams, internal product/eng)

- 
 Comfortable operating with technical ambiguity -- you don't need to write code, but you need to understand SDK gaps, integration patterns, and technical GTM stories well enough to be credible with SAs and engineers

- 
 Strong program management instincts -- this role is equal parts relationship-building and disciplined execution (gap analyses, joint plans, quarterly business reviews, and pipeline tracking)

- 
 Proven ability to execute co-marketing and co-sell initiatives that impact the bottom line, paired with a deep understanding of partner attribution and reporting

- 
 High degree of autonomy and external credibility—you lead your own workstreams, close loops, and represent Supabase in high-stakes partner discussions independently

- 
 Experience with AWS Partner Central, ACE, and Marketplace mechanics is a plus.

 What We Offer 

- 
 Fully Remote 

 We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

- 
 ESOP 

 Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

- 
 Tech Allowance 

 Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

- 
 Health Benefits 

 Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

- 
 Annual Off-Sites 

 Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

- 
 Flexible Work 

 We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

- 
 Professional Development 

 Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

 About the Team 

 Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

- 
 ~400 team members

- 
 60+ countries

- 
 20+ languages spoken

- 
 Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

- 
 540,000+ community members

 We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Job Description
Main challenge 
 We're launching preproduction on a new project built on Unreal Engine. Your role: be the person who can dive deep under the hood of the engine to understand why something isn't working — and the one who sets the best practices so the whole team gets the most out of it.
 What it means on a daily basis 
 You’ll know the engine well enough to open it up, find what’s really going on, and turn every fix into a practice the whole team can build on:
 
- Become the team's go-to Unreal Engine expert and the GPP leads' technical partner on defining coding standards

- Develop the engine systems the game needs in C++, in direct support of the GPP team

- Diagnose and fix existing technical issues — and get ahead of the next ones

- Own console TRC compliance across every platform

- Set up a performance-tracking system, drawing on Unreal's testing APIs or Gauntlet

- Monitor performance through Unreal Insights and share your recommendations with the GPPs
 What success will look like 
 The GPPs come to you naturally and know they can count on you. Your documentation on engine processes and best practices becomes a go-to reference for the team, you've taken ownership of TRC and performance issues, and you know how to dive deep into the engine whenever it's needed.
 Who you would be working with 
 You'll report to our Gameplay Director, work closely with our Gameplay Lead, Studio Technical Director and the whole GPP team.

Qualifications
Who you are 
 You’re the person teammates come to when things get stuck, and you like leaving them better equipped than you found them.
 
- You’re a natural evangelist for best practices, and you enjoy teaching as much as solving.

- You’re the technical firefighter people call in a tight spot, and you stay calm because you want to understand why something works before working around it.

- You stay curious and rigorous, and you’re open to feedback, never set in your own certainties.
 What you need to succeed 
 You’ve spent real time under Unreal’s hood, and you’re comfortable when the answer isn’t in the docs.
 
- Strong C++ and Unreal Engine experience, with a genuine appetite for digging into the engine itself.

- Knowledge of console TRC and their technical requirements.

- Hands-on experience with Unreal Insights for performance diagnostics.

- Professional French and English, since English is increasingly used day to day.

- A plus: familiarity with Unreal’s rendering stack and rendering-oriented performance.
 Your recruitment journey 
 
- First interview: with our HR Manager

- Test: CodinGames exercise

- Second interview: with our Technical Director and our Lead Gameplay

- Third interview: with our Game Manager and Studio Manager
 Where this role can take you 
 By building recognized engine expertise on Unreal, you're set to become the studio's technical reference on the subject — with real potential to grow into a lead or engine architect role.

job.description:
Job Description
WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON​ 
 What you will focus on 
 This role exists because reactive execution is no longer enough. The OTT programming division needs a technical authority who can shift the team's positioning from "a team that delivers what it is asked to build" to "a technical partners that others actively seek out because of the value it brings to a game's success." That shift requires someone who can set a long-term technical vision, build scalable production ecosystems, and drive focused R&D including applied AI in game development, while simultaneously ensuring flawless deliveries across multiple live and co-development projects.
  
 What it means on a daily basis​ 
 
- Monitor the technical health of multiple projects, working closely with technical leads to surface risks early, prevent bottlenecks, and keep deliveries on track.

- Define and enforce studio-wide coding standards, architectural patterns, and engineering workflows, and drive their adoption across programming teams.

- Lead high-impact R&D initiatives, with particular focus on AI applied to game development, and ensure successful integration of outcomes into production pipelines.

- Provide hands-on technical guidance and mentoring to programmers, conducting periodic competency assessments and building clear development paths.

- Act as the primary technical counterpart for co-development partner studios, aligning on architecture, tooling, style guides, and Unreal toolchain standardization across shared pipelines.

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Game Design, Art, and Production to improve how programming integrates with other disciplines and contributes to overall product quality.

- Strategic resource planning and project allocation in partnership with the Studio Technical Director.
  
 What success will look like​ 
 Within your first year, you will have made a visible and assessable impact on at least one co-development project or on a strategic technical mission defined in alignment with the studio's long-term vision. That impact will be confirmed through calibration with multiple stakeholders across the organization, not through self-assessment alone.
  
 Who you would be working with​ 
 
- Report to the Studio Technical Director.

- Operate accross a programming department of around 35 to 40 people, spanning multiple seniority levels and allocated to live service and co-development projects.

- Collaborate closely with Department Heads and Team Leads across Game Design, Art, and Production, as well as Studio Directors and the Studio Manager.

- Work directly with Technical Managers and Technical Directors from co-development partner studios.
  
 Your recruitment journey 
 
- Screen Call with a Recruiter

- First Interview  with the Studio Technical Director and Division Principal/Manager

- Second Interview with Studio Manager and HR Director 

- Final interview with a Technical Director from a sister studio
  
 Where this role can take you 
 If the opportunity arises and the qualifications are in place, this position is a direct pathway to the Studio Technical Director role. That outcome is not guaranteed, but it is a realistic evolution for the right person.

Qualifications
WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED​ 
 
- Proven hands-on expertise in game development across multiple genres and platforms, including  mobile, PC, and console. 

- High proficiency in Unreal Engine 5 and programming languages such as C++ and C# .

- Demonstrated ability to design and lead large-scale technical systems , covering areas such as 3D rendering, AI gameplay systems, online and network scalability, and cloud infrastructure.

- A track record of leading R&D initiatives from exploration through to production integration.

- Demonstrated leadership of multi-disciplinary programming teams, including identifying skill gaps, building development plans, and raising the collective output quality of a department rather than just individual projects.

- The ability to communicate technical direction clearly to senior leadership, partner studio counterparts, and non-technical collaborators, and to influence decisions at a strategic level while maintaining alignment across stakeholders.

- Practical experience deploying AI and LLM-based tools in a production context.
  
 WHO YOU ARE

job.description:
Job Description
WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON 
 The Gametech Innovation team builds the tools and systems Gameloft’s game teams work with, from AI in production pipelines to art pipeline optimisation across Unity and Unreal. We are looking for a Tech Lead to take technical ownership of that work as the team continues to grow its scope. You will be responsible for the architecture, establish quality standards, and work directly with the studios using the team’s solutions.
 What it means on a daily basis 
 
- Evaluate new engine features, technologies and AI capabilities, then define the architecture and technology choices the team commits to across Unity and Unreal projects

- Work closely on complex features and essential systems using C++ and C#

- Own technical quality: coding standards, code reviews, build and release pipelines, and how AI is integrated into both our tools and our own development workflow

- Mentor developers on architecture, design decisions and code quality, through reviews, pairing and technical discussion

- Work with studios to understand what actually slows them down, turn that into feasible technical scopes and estimates, and flag technical risks early enough to do something about them
 What success will look like 
 In the beginning, it means getting familiar with the codebases, connecting with the studios the team supports, and identifying the most urgent areas to address. As you settle in, you will have set the architecture direction for the team’s main projects and established how technical quality is held. Later on, the benchmark is straightforward: studios use the team’s tools every day, and the developers around you are making more effective technical choices without needing much guidance.
 Who you would be working with 
 You will be reporting to our Gametech Innovation Manager, and collaborate very closely with other Developers from the Gametech Innovation team across multiple studios worldwide, including Paris, Montreal, Bucharest, and others, offering opportunities to collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Day to day you will work with game programmers, technical artists and producers on Gameloft's game teams internationally.
 Your recruitment journey 
 
- Recruitment interview: A conversation to explore how the role aligns with your background and to address your main questions.

- HM interview: You will meet a Hiring Manager to discuss your experience, vision, and how you approach game technology topics at a broader level.

- Test: You will receive a short case study to complete.

- Tech interview: You will meet members of our technical team to present your test and talk through your approach, reasoning, and methodologies in more depth.
 Where this role can take you 
 Over time, and depending on your interests and the team’s needs, this role can grow in two directions: towards people management as the team expands, or towards architecture and technical direction across our projects and studios. Training, mentorship and coaching programmes are available along the way, and Talent Move lets you look at internal opportunities elsewhere at Gameloft.

Qualifications
WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED 
 
- Advanced proficiency with Unreal Engine and/or Unity, including their editors and extensions, and solid proficiency in C++ and C#

- Experience building and launching tools or systems that other teams relied on and kept using

- Advanced debugging, profiling and performance optimisation across complex systems, together with the ability to write clean, maintainable and self-explanatory code

- Solid understanding of CI/CD, build infrastructure and version control at scale

- Practical use of AI in real development work, both as coding assistants in your own workflow and as services integrated into the tools you build
 WHO YOU ARE 
 
- Curious: you enjoy digging into unfamiliar problems and exploring new engines, tools and approaches

- Solution-driven: you turn ambiguous requests into workable technical paths and treat constraints as problems to solve

- A mentor: you raise the technical level around you through code review, pairing and design discussion, and explain your reasoning clearly in English to technical and non-technical people alike

Additional Information
WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU 
 Benefits 
 
- Remote work: Up to 2 days per week, plus up to 1 month of full remote work from anywhere in France and up to 1 month abroad each year.

- Access to Wellpass (formerly Gymlib)

- Employee Savings Plan (PEG) 

- Standard benefits: meal vouchers, 50% reimbursement of public transportation costs (Navigo pass), and health insurance
 Life at Gameloft 
 We believe that great work starts with a stimulating and supportive environment. That's why we offer flexible working hours, unlimited coffee and tea, fresh fruit, and monthly breakfast gatherings to help kick-start the day.
 Our offices are also designed to encourage collaboration and team spirit, with dedicated spaces for video games and board games, foosball and ping-pong tables, as well as weekly futsal sessions. And of course, you'll have plenty of opportunities to connect through our regular company events!
 Ready to join the game? Apply now!

job.description:
Description du poste
Gameloft Montréal recherche un(e) Artiste technique pour rejoindre l'équipe qui travaille sur Disney Dreamlight Valley, un jeu hybride de simulation de vie et d'aventure multiplateforme !
 Rempli de quêtes, d'exploration et d'activités captivantes avec des personnages emblématiques de Disney et Pixar, Disney Dreamlight Valley est une production originale de Gameloft Montréal créée par une équipe passionnée impatiente de vous accueillir !
 Pour en savoir plus sur le jeu : 

 Bande-annonce : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hdvh9ninISE 

 Site officiel :  https://disneydreamlightvalley.com/ 
 Sous la supervision du Chef technique, et en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de programmation et artistique, l'Artiste technique conçoit des outils et développe un pipeline de production graphique optimal pour soutenir le processus de création de son équipe pour le contenu actuel et à venir. Il ou elle veille à répondre à toutes les attentes artistiques et de design, dans le respect des contraintes de performance et des délais de production.
 Principales tâches et responsabilités 
 Pipeline et outils 
 
- Superviser et tenir à jour le pipeline des ressources artistiques, et détecter les problèmes avant qu'ils n'atteignent une version.

- Développer et tenir à jour des outils de création numérique qui appliquent les conventions de nomenclature, les budgets de triangles, les dispositions UV, etc.

- Créer et maintenir les paramètres d'importation côté moteur (modèles, compression des textures, etc.).
 Performance et optimisation 
 
- Établir des budgets par asset (nombre de triangles, densité de texels, nombre de matériaux, etc.) par scène ou par classe d'assets, et vérifier les nouvelles soumissions d'assets par rapport à ces budgets avant que les dépassements ne s'accumulent dans tout le projet.

- Profiler les versions sur le matériel cible et traduire les résultats en étapes exploitables.

- Optimiser des assets spécifiques en cas de besoin.
 Shaders et matériaux 
 
- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les programmeurs graphiques pour créer et tenir à jour la bibliothèque de shaders du projet en utilisant à la fois le Shader Graph et le HLSL.

- Collaborer avec le Directeur artistique pour prototyper de nouveaux effets visuels et travailler avec l'équipe artistique pour les intégrer au projet.

- Examiner et corriger les bugs de matériaux/shaders (artefacts de profondeur et de tri, artefacts de mosaïquage, réponse PBR incorrecte, etc.).

- Valider les configurations de matériaux dans différentes conditions d'éclairage et sur les plateformes cibles.
 Normes de l'équipe artistique 
 
- Rédiger et mettre à jour les sections techniques du guide artistique (conventions de nomenclature, spécifications d'exportation, formats de textures, structure des dossiers, considérations d'optimisation, etc.), qui sont cruciales pour les artistes internes et les partenaires en sous-traitance.

- Former les nouveaux artistes aux outils de pipeline et appliquer les normes.

- Assumer le triage initial de tous les problèmes d'intégration des ressources.

- Définir et spécifier les demandes et caractéristiques du nouveau pipeline artistique.

- Évaluer et recommander de nouveaux outils, plugins et mises à niveau du pipeline.
 ---
 Gameloft Montreal is looking for a Technical Artist to join the team working on Disney Dreamlight Valley, a cross-platform hybrid life-sim/adventure game!
 Filled with quests, exploration, and engaging activities featuring iconic Disney and Pixar characters, Disney Dreamlight Valley is an original Gameloft Montreal production created by a passionate team eager to welcome you!
 To learn more about the game: 

 Trailer:  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hdvh9ninISE 

 Official website:  https://disneydreamlightvalley.com/ 
 Under the supervision of the technical lead, and working closely with the programming and art teams, the technical artist designs tools and develops an optimal graphics production pipeline to support their team's creation process for existing and upcoming content. They make sure to meet any artistic/design expectations, in keeping with performance constraints and production deadlines.
 Main Tasks and Responsibilities 
 Pipeline & Tooling 
 
- Monitor and maintain the art asset pipeline, and catch issues before they reach a build.

- Write and maintain DCC tools that enforce naming conventions, triangle budgets, UV layouts, etc.

- Author and maintain engine-side import settings (models, texture compression, etc.).
 Performance & Optimization 
 
- Establish per-asset budgets (triangle count, texel density, material count, etc.) per scene or asset class, and audit new asset submissions against them before violations compound across the project.

- Profile builds on target hardware and translate the findings into actionable steps.

- Optimize specific assets when needed.
 Shaders & Materials 
 
- Work closely with the Graphics Programmers to author and maintain the project shader library using both Shader Graph and HLSL.

- Collaborate with the Art Director to prototype new visual effects and work with the art team to integrate them in the project.

- Investigate and fix material/shader bugs (depth and sorting artifacts, tiling artifacts, incorrect PBR response, etc.).

- Validate material setups across lighting conditions and target platforms.
 Art Team Standards 
 
- Write and maintain the Art Bible's technical sections (naming conventions, export specs, texture formats, folder structure, optimization considerations, etc.), which are critical for internal artists and outsourcing partners.

- Onboard new artists to pipeline tools and enforce standards.

- Own first-response triage for all art-to-engine issues.

- Scope and spec new art pipeline requests and features.

- Evaluate and recommend new tools, plugins, and pipeline upgrades.

Qualifications
- Expérience de contribution à un pipeline artistique sur un projet livré

- Expérience de publication sur au moins une plateforme console (Nintendo Switch™, PS5® ou Xbox Series) et expérience pratique avec les contraintes spécifiques à la mémoire et aux shaders de la plateforme

- Compétence avec Git et SVN, et à l'aise avec les flux de travail basés sur les demandes de fusion
 Moteur et pipeline 
 
- Solide compétence avec Unity (URP), avec une expérience pratique dans plusieurs de ses systèmes (rendu, pipeline d'assets, profilage, débogage)

- Compétence en C# pour les outils d'éditeur (inspecteurs personnalisés, validateurs, traitements en lots)

- Expérience en rédaction ou maintenance d'outils de validation d'assets

- À l'aise avec le travail sur les préréglages d'importation et les substitutions de plateforme (compression des textures, compression des maillages)
 Outils de création numérique 
 
- Expérience de l'écriture de scripts dans au moins un des langages suivants : 3ds Max, Blender ou Maya (exportateurs, outils par lots, validation, nettoyage de scènes)

- Familiarité avec les flux de travail de Substance 3D Painter/Designer
 Shaders et matériaux 
 
- Solide expérience en HLSL dans URP, y compris les shaders personnalisés illuminés/non illuminés et les mots-clés de shader

- À l'aise avec Shader Graph et comprend quand l'écriture manuelle en HLSL est une meilleure option

- Bonne compréhension de la PBR, des espaces colorimétriques et du comportement de l'éclairage sur les différentes plateformes

- Expérience de débogage des problèmes de shaders sur diverses plateformes
 Performance et profilage 
 
- Expérience pratique avec les outils de profilage et de débogage GPU tels que Unity Frame Debugger et Nsight, et capable de lire une capture d'image fixe pour identifier les goulots d'étranglement GPU courants (appels de dessin, taux de remplissage, coûts des shaders)

- Expérience de travail avec des budgets par asset et par scène (triangles, densité des texels, nombre de matériaux, surdessin, mémoire) et pour les faire respecter
 Normes et communication 
 
- Expérience dans la rédaction et la mise à jour de la documentation technique liée à l'art (sections du guide artistique, guides des pipelines)

- À l'aise pour guider les artistes sur les meilleures pratiques techniques et examiner leur travail quant à la conformité au pipeline

- À l'aise en tant que premier point de contact pour les artistes rencontrant des problèmes avec le moteur

- Capable de définir la portée d'une demande de fonctionnalité pour un pipeline, rédiger une spécification succincte, l'évaluer et la livrer
 Atouts 
 
- Expérience dans le soutien des pipelines d'installation et d'animation (résolution de problèmes et révision de contenu)

- Expérience dans le soutien des effets visuels (résolution de problèmes, optimisation et révision de contenu)

- Familiarité avec Houdini (pipelines procéduraux, HDA) ou autres outils de contenu procédural

- Expérience avec les shaders de calcul (systèmes d'herbe/particules, instanciation GPU, dessin indirect, etc.)

- Expérience avec les pipelines d'éclairage (sondes lumineuses, flux de travail de cuisson, outils d'auteur de sondes)

- Familiarité avec Jira/Confluence pour la gestion des problèmes et le pipeline de documentation

- Expérience précédente en tant qu'artiste avant de passer à l'art technique
 ---
 
- Experience contributing to an art pipeline on a shipped project

- Experience shipping on at least one console platform (Nintendo Switch™, PS5® or Xbox Series) and hands-on experience with platform-specific memory and shader constraints

- Proficient with Git and SVN, and comfortable with merge-request-based workflows
 Engine & Pipeline 
 
- Strong Unity proficiency (URP), with hands-on experience in several of its systems (rendering, asset pipeline, profiling, debugging)

- Proficient in C# for editor tooling (custom inspectors, validators, batch processors)

- Experience writing or maintaining asset validation tools

- Comfortable working with import presets and platform overrides (texture compression, mesh compression)
 DCC Tools 
 
- Experience writing scripts in at least one of the following: 3ds Max, Blender, or Maya (exporters, batch tools, validation, scene cleanup)

- Familiarity with Substance 3D Painter/Designer workflows
 Shaders & Materials 
 
- Solid HLSL experience in URP, including custom lit/unlit shaders and shader keywords

- Comfortable in Shader Graph and understands when handwritten HLSL is a better option

- Good understanding of PBR, color spaces, and how lighting behaves across platforms

- Experience debugging shader issues across platforms
 Performance & Profiling 
 
- Hands-on experience with GPU profiling and debugging tools such as Unity Frame Debugger and Nsight, and able to read a frame capture to identify common GPU bottlenecks (draw calls, fillrate, shader costs)

- Experience working with per-asset and per-scene budgets (triangles, texel density, material count, overdraw, memory) and helping enforce them
 Standards & Communication 
 
- Experience writing and maintaining technical art documentation (Art Bible sections, pipeline guides)

- Comfortable guiding artists on technical best practices and reviewing their work for pipeline compliance

- Comfortable as the first point of contact for artists who have encountered engine issues

- Able to scope a pipeline feature request, write a short spec, estimate, and ship it
 Nice to Have 
 
- Experience supporting rigging and animation pipelines (troubleshooting issues and content review)

- Experience supporting VFX (troubleshooting, optimization and content review)

- Familiarity with Houdini (procedural pipelines, HDAs) or other procedural content tools

- Compute shader experience (grass/particle systems, GPU instancing, indirect draw, etc.)

- Experience with lighting pipelines (light probes, baking workflows, probe authoring tools)

- Familiarity with Jira/Confluence for issue triage and pipeline documentation

- Previous experience as an artist before moving into tech art

Informations supplémentaires
Ce en quoi Gameloft croit : 
 Nous jouons le jeu pour un monde meilleur. En tant que leader dans l'industrie, nous voulons utiliser le pouvoir des jeux vidéos comme une force positive au changement.

En nous rejoignant, vous aurez une multitudes d'opportunités pour aider votre environnement, faire la différence et bâtir un monde plus inclusif.
 Nous voulons que les Gamelofteurs se concentrent sur l'essentiel: créer du fun et des jeux de haute qualité dont ils pourront être fiers de les partager avec les joueurs du monde entier.
 Pour vous aider dans votre rôle, nous avons mis en place les bénéfices suivants:

- Vendredi après-midi de congé toute l’année!

 Mais aussi au studio :

job.description:
Job Description
WHAT YOU WILL BE WORKING ON 

 The Gametech Innovation team is a specialized group of developers focused on empowering Gameloft’s game teams to create better games through innovative technological solutions. We focus on Unity and Unreal engines, developing tools and systems that span a wide range of game development needs.

As a Mid-Level Developer within the team, you will manage feature delivery and support the technical stability of our tools and systems, contributing to the full lifecycle of each solution.
 What it means on a daily basis 
 
- Own features or subsystems end-to-end, from benchmarking existing solutions and prototyping alternatives through to implementing and shipping the final tool to game teams

- Write maintainable, self-explanatory code in C++ and C# within Unreal and Unity engines

- Debug and profile tools and systems across engines and target platforms (console, PC, mobile) so they stay reliable in production

- Maintain and extend the team's CI/CD and build pipelines so new tool versions reach game teams continuously

- Use AI coding assistants in your daily workflow, experiment with new approaches and technologies, and propose the incremental improvements worth industrialising
 What success will look like 
 In your first three months, you will be at ease in the team's codebase and delivering fixes and features on existing tools with limited guidance. From there, you will own a feature or subsystem end-to-end, you will propose improvements to tools and workflows on your own initiative and become a technical point of contact for the game teams we support.
 Who you would be working with 
 You will be reporting to our Gametech Innovation Manager, and collaborate very closely with other Developers from the Gametech Innovation team across multiple studios worldwide, including Paris, Montreal, Bucharest, and others, offering opportunities to collaborate with colleagues from diverse backgrounds and perspectives. Day to day you will work with game programmers, technical artists and producers on Gameloft's game teams internationally.
 Your recruitment journey 
 
- First interview: A conversation to explore how the role aligns with your background and to address your main questions.

- Test: You will receive a short case study to complete.

- Second interview: You will meet members of our technical team to present your test and talk through your approach, reasoning, and methodologies in more depth.

- Final interview: You will meet a Hiring Manager to discuss your experience, vision, and how you approach game technology topics at a broader level.
 Where this role can take you 
 This role can be a stepping stone toward a more senior position within the Gametech Innovation team, or toward specialising in a particular area such as engine, pipeline or platform technology. Internal training and mentoring from the team's senior developers are available, and internal mobility across teams and studios is possible through Gameloft's Talent Move programme.

Qualifications
WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED 
 
- Solid proficiency with Unreal Engine and/or Unity; and in C++ and C#

- Practical use of AI coding assistants in your day-to-day development work

- Good debugging and profiling skills across multiple systems, together with the ability to write clean, maintainable and self-explanatory code

- Working knowledge of CI/CD and build pipelines
 WHO YOU ARE 
 
- Naturally curious: you enjoy digging into unfamiliar problems and exploring new engines, tools and approaches

- Solution-driven: you turn ambiguous, poorly defined requests into workable technical paths, treat constraints as problems to solve, and propose improvements beyond your assigned scope to keep the team moving forward

Additional Information
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU​ 
 Benefits 
 
- Permanent contract, full-time employment with comprehensive Social Benefits.

- 25 vacation days per year + Birthday day off.

- Private medical health insurance.

- Flexible compensation with Ticket Restaurant Card.

- Free language courses.

- Work-from-home hybrid model.

- Merit based salary progression system and a competitive initial salary package.

 Life at Gameloft  
 Our Barcelona studio offers real career development opportunities and a positive working environment in a centrally located office. We value supportive working conditions and a balanced work-life approach, and our teams work together with a collaborative mindset.

 Ready to level up your career? Apply now with your CV in English.

Who We Are:

NaturalMotion is an award-winning UK game studio dedicated to crafting world-class mobile experiences. Alongside our continued live-service development on CSR Racing 2 (#1 drag racing series of all time), our team is stepping into its next chapter with an ambitious, unannounced project. Honoured for eight consecutive years as a GamesIndustry.biz Best Place to Work in the UK winner and named a Top 50 UK Game Maker in 2025 and 2026, we offer a collaborative studio culture backed by the global reach of Zynga and Take-Two Interactive.

Position Overview:

We are seeking a Server & Infrastructure Engineer to join our server engineering team. In this role, you will work on core backend systems and backend services, contributing directly to live services and build systems with minimal supervision. You will help manage and expand our infrastructure, automated CI/CD pipelines, and development tools while collaborating closely with technical leads to build reliable, high-performing server environments. You will have a passion for large-scale high-availability systems, a devotion to software craftsmanship, an unwavering commitment to quality, and the desire to have their work seen by tens of millions of people worldwide.

We embrace a hybrid work environment. Within this role, you would work 2 days per week in our London office and the remaining days at home.

What You'll Do:

  • Server & Infrastructure Execution: Complete multi-day backend engineering tasks with minimal guidance. Design, deploy, and support scalable server architectures and cloud infrastructure.
  • DevOps & Pipeline Automation: Build, maintain, and optimise robust CI/CD workflows and automated deployment pipelines across cloud environments and build platforms.
  • Architecture & Planning: Participate in technical planning, architectural brainstorming, and technical cost/complexity estimation for multi-week efforts.
  • Team Efficiency & Quality: Proactively identify workflow bottlenecks and drive initiatives to improve overall engineering team productivity, tooling, and code quality.
  • Technical Communication: Participate in internal tech talks, share best practices, and maintain collaborative peer relationships across engineering squads.

What You Bring:

  • Programming Languages: Demonstrated proficiency in Python, Go and C# for backend services, automation scripts, and custom tooling.
  • Cloud Infrastructure & IaC: Hands-on experience provisioning and managing AWS infrastructure using Terraform (Infrastructure as Code).
  • Build & Platform Systems: Experience configuring and managing automated orchestration/build platforms (e.g., Unreal Horde, Jenkins, or TeamCity), preferably with Game Engines (Unreal Engine, Unity, etc.).
  • Source Control Management: Strong working knowledge of version control systems and workflow strategies (GitHub, Perforce/Helix Core, Git-flow, branch management).
  • Work Execution: Proven ability to manage moderate-to-complex technical tasks independently, break down project deliverables, and communicate status accurately.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience writing server-side logic and managing database dependencies for live applications or multiplayer services.
  • Have worked in, or has a strong interest in the gaming industry
  • Interest in infrastructure deployment and monitoring
  • Interest in mentoring junior team members or interns, framing task deconstruction, and conducting technical interviews.
  • Familiarity with containerisation (Docker, Kubernetes) and infrastructure security best practices.

What We Offer You: 

  • Competitive salary and discretionary annual bonus scheme
  • 26 days holiday, plus bank holidays & 2 paid personal days
  • 6 months fully paid maternity/adoption leave and 16 weeks fully paid paternity leave (eligibility criteria applies)
  • Pension plan, with a double matching employer contribution

  • Fitness reimbursement plan, worth £600 per annum
  • Flexible working hours
  • Weekly happy hours, seasonal parties and monthly social events
  • Annual rail season ticket advance and cycle to work scheme

job.description:
Homa is a global mobile game developer and publisher creating games people love. We partner with studios and internally develop games, having launched over 80 titles, reached over 2 billion downloads, and seen our game All in Hole break into the global top-50 grossing charts. These are milestones, not the finish line.
 With deep expertise in product and technology, we built Homa Lab, our proprietary platform that gives developers the market intelligence, data tools, and game tech, with AI built in, to find product–market fit fast and scale mass-market games into lasting experiences players enjoy for years.
 This is our flywheel: Homa Lab helps studios spot the right ideas early, turn them into games quickly, and reach millions of players. Every launch brings back data and insights that fuel the next hit, making each turn of the loop faster, smarter, and more likely to win. AI supercharges this process, running through everything we do, from everyday tasks to our guiding principles.
 What powers the loop is talent density. 220+ people from 30+ nationalities, bringing expertise from the world's best studios and companies. We uphold ambition, curiosity, humility, and focus, and deliver with speed, excellence, and candor.
 Since the start, we've raised $165M from Headline, Northzone, Eurazeo, Bpifrance, and the founders of King, Sorare, and Spotify, people who've built and backed the games and platforms we admire, now supporting our drive to create the next ones.
 At Homa, we are building the next billion-player experiences from the ground up and shaping the future of entertainment.
 The opportunity
 As an AI Unity Tools Engineer, you'll build the next generation of QA automation and development tooling for Homa's games. This is a new, high-impact initiative, and you'll own it: from the first question to the tools running in production across our portfolio.
 You’ll work across AI, Unity, QA automation, DevOps, and infrastructure to make testing and build pipelines more reliable, scalable, and cost-efficient for games developed by Homa and its studios. You'll be working on AI-driven QA automation at the edge of what is technically possible, and you'll see the impact directly in the speed, reliability, and cost of how our games are made.

What you'll do
 
- Build. Design and deploy AI-enabled QA automation pipelines across Homa's major Unity games.

- Run. Maintain and improve our TeamCity build pipelines and infrastructure so game builds stay reliable.

- Scale. Onboard new games and tools onto the platform without reducing service quality.

- Explore. Test AI-driven approaches to QA that cut manual testing effort and reduce reliance on costly legacy tooling.

- Drive adoption. Work with developers, QA teams, studios, and mobile teams so the tools you build are actually used.

- Measure. Track the impact of your work on testing time, build reliability, and cost, and turn it into clear recommendations.
 Requirements 
 
- Ownership. You drive outcomes. When a build breaks or a test fails, you fix it instead of explaining why it broke.

- Proactive. You don't wait for instructions or perfect conditions. You spot what needs doing and do it.

- Pragmatism and simplicity. You look for the simplest solution that works, use whatever tools are available, and ship. You turn ambitious ideas into practical, achievable solutions.

- Sharp thinking. You learn fast, reason from facts, and structure your ideas clearly. You can explain a complex technical solution to developers, QA teams, and studios in a few sentences.

- AI-driven. AI is already part of how you work every day. You've used it to automate, speed up, or rethink at least one thing you're proud of.

- Hungry and motivated. You're ambitious, high-energy, and grounded. You see this role as a chance to build something new and grow faster than anywhere else, and you're ready to work for it.

- Bonus: you've built something. An internal tool, a testing framework, a game, a side project. We'd love to hear about it.
 For this role, you'll also bring
 
- Hands-on experience with Unity and the ability to understand Unity games, game systems, and testing contexts.

- Proven experience using AI systems, models, or AI-enabled engineering workflows in practice.

- Strong DevOps understanding, including TeamCity, build pipelines, and infrastructure.

- The ability to work across technical topics while understanding the wider product and business context.

- Experience working in a complex environment with meaningful product and testing volumes.
 Bonus points if you have:
 
- Experience building QA automation or testing frameworks.

- Experience with AI-driven exploratory testing.

- Experience in gaming or another Unity-based product environment.

- Experience supporting products with high testing volumes.

- Experience driving adoption of internal tools across multiple teams.
 Even if you don't check every box, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.
 
 Why Homa
 
- Exceptional growth. We hire people of outstanding potential, then put them where they can grow fastest.

- Real ownership, early. This is a new initiative. Your tools will change how Homa and its studios build and test games, and you'll see the results.

- A high talent bar. Our teams are small and demanding, and the people around you will push you to grow.

- AI at the core. You'll have access to the best AI tools, and you'll help shape how an AI-first company works.
 Benefits 
 Building great games starts with building a great place to work. Here's what you can expect:
 
- 🏥 Comprehensive Benefits: Depending on your location, you'll enjoy a range of perks such as insurance, meal vouchers, public transport, gym memberships, and more.

- 🏢 Paris HQ Access: Enjoy a desk at our private office in a well-located WeWork building that will give you access to WeWork perks like rooftop view and designed coworking spaces.

- 🌍 Coworking Access: You will have access to WeWork spaces throughout Europe, along with all their perks and professional office environments.

- 🌐 Global Team: Collaborate in English with top-tier talent from 35+ countries, spanning Europe, the UK, the US, and more. Diversity fuels our creativity and innovation.

- ✈️ Team Gatherings: We value time together beyond the screen. Join us for occasional team gatherings, off-site retreats (Workations as we name them) to connect, recharge, and celebrate.

- 📈 Performance Reviews: We're committed to your growth. Every six months, we reflect on your progress, recognize your achievements, and align on clear development goals.

- 💻 Equipment Support: From day one, we'll provide everything you need to do your best work, including a home office setup allowance if you're working remotely.
 Where We Hire
 Our HQ in Paris is a vibrant hub of creativity, collaboration, and connection. From rooftop lunches and coffee chats to after-work apéros and community events, we've designed a space people genuinely enjoy - all within a cosy WeWork filled with good energy (and snacks).

job.description:
Job Description
As a Senior C++ Engine Programmer at Ubisoft Montréal, you’ll join the Core Services - Online Tech Foundations team. The team builds technology that supports online services across many Ubisoft productions. You’ll help design and evolve distributed systems and middleware used in games, including game engine, low-level, networking, and engine-integrated web components.
 What you’ll do 
 
- Develop and improve reliable, high-performing, maintainable C++ middleware.

- Contribute to technical direction and architecture choices.

- Improve code quality through good practices, code reviews, and continuous improvement.

- Solve complex technical problems and optimize performance.

- Reduce risks and technical debt to help keep solutions sustainable.

- Collaborate with teams and other stakeholders.

- Share knowledge and keep up with technical developments.

Qualifications
What you bring to the team 
 
- Advanced proficiency in modern C++ (C++17/20/23 and beyond).

- Strong expertise in software architecture and complex systems.

- Deep low-level programming knowledge (memory management, multithreading, CPU optimization).

- Ability to design high-performance algorithms and optimized data structures.

- Excellent debugging and profiling skills.

- Proficiency with Continuous Integration and Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) practices and tools.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities for complex challenges.

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

- Self-driven, proactive, and highly autonomous.

- Strong attention to detail and quality-oriented mindset.

- Ability to influence technical decisions and strategic directions.

 Assets : 
 
- Console development experience (PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch).

- Expertise in C#.

- Experience with one or more game engines (Snowdrop, Anvil, Unreal Engine, Unity).

- Knowledge of cloud infrastructure and services (AWS, Azure).

- Experience working on game productions with significant online/multiplayer components.

- Advanced technical expertise in areas such as online services and networking

Additional Information


Company Description
Ubisoft is a global leader in gaming with teams across the world creating original and memorable gaming experiences, from Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six to Just Dance and more. We believe diverse perspectives help both players and teams thrive. If you’re passionate about innovation and pushing entertainment boundaries, join our journey and help create the unknown!

I'm applying for the Online Programmer - OS (Game Network) role at Ubisoft. I currently work at Phibonacci Solution, Ahmedabad.

What I would bring to this role:
- Unity 3D (incl. Unity 6) and C#: clean, reusable production code across seven studios, from idea to launch
- Gameplay systems, game mechanics and scene management
- Multiplayer systems with Socket.IO real-time networking and REST API integration
- Performance: Unity Profiler, memory optimization, object pooling and draw-call optimization

I'm based in India and open to relocating to Montreal for this role.

Portfolio: https://denishmakadiya-unity.github.io/
GitHub: https://github.com/denishmakadiya-unity
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/denish-makadiya-a0b776ab

My resume is attached. I'd welcome a short conversation about how I can help.

Job Description
As a Senior Technical Artist - Characters (Unreal) at Ubisoft Montréal , you will be the point of reference for technical matters related to character content creation, from concept handoff through in-engine integration. You will define how characters are produced on the project and put the end-to-end pipeline in place. You will guide the resolution of complex issues across modeling, texturing, rigging, skinning, and runtime integration, while advising on the project’s broader technical direction.
 What you’ll do 
 
- Identify technical needs across character creation, rigging, skinning, levels of detail, materials, and engine integration

- Shape the character technology vision with technical directors and associate technical directors, in line with the art and animation vision

- Define the character pipeline , including creation-to-engine workflows, naming and export conventions, and validation steps

- Set and share character standards for asset structure, versioning, rigs, skeletons, materials, and textures

- Create or recommend tools for character artists, riggers, and animators, including export automation, asset validators, rig builders, and batch processing utilities

- Optimize and debug character assets for geometry, draw calls, skinning cost, memory use, and shader complexity

- Resolve complex character issues , including deformation quality, cloth and hair integration, and modular character systems

- Collaborate with animation and programming teams on character features and runtime systems, and communicate progress to associates and technical directors

- Document standards and tools , follow developments in character technology, help align teams around shared goals, and contribute to performance evaluations within the specialty

Qualifications
What you bring to the team 
 
- Hands-on experience with an end-to-end character pipeline , including how character assets are created and integrated into a game engine

- Knowledge of rigging and animation needs sufficient to guide the pipeline and work with animation teams

- Knowledge of technical budgets , polygon counts, materials, asset structure, and modular character customization

- Experience establishing workflows and standards for character production

- Experience with Unreal Engine 5 , or relevant character pipeline experience with Unreal Engine 4
 What to send our way 
 
- Send your CV highlighting relevant skills and experience

- Share a portfolio or links to relevant projects

job.description:
Job Description
The Technical Artist is a key support role within the Rainbow Six: Siege team, working closely with other Technical Artists as well as 3D, Texture, Concept, and Character Artists. This role bridges the gap between the artistic and technical aspects of asset production, ensuring that all assets—such as uniforms, headgear, charms, weapons, and other customization items—are efficiently integrated into the game engine. 
 In addition, the Technical Artist contributes to asset and pipeline optimization, tool development, and technical setup and validation processes, maintaining high-quality visuals while ensuring optimal performance across all in-game content. 
  
 Key Responsibilities: 
 
- Derisk 3D concepts: List of checks that needs to respect guidelines for 2D and 3D assets that include clipping, neck connection, skin meshes compatibility, mem budget, collision meshes, tattoos, hair, gadget, legs, shoes).

- Tech Validation: List of checks, adjustments and corrections for all 2D and 3D assets that include meshes (hands, body, neck, eyes, straps, etc), collision meshes, skeleton (pivot points), mem budgets, UVs, textures (color mask, albedo, roughness, metalness, normals, emissive). Have ownership of asset approvals for tech guidelines compliance. 

- Tech Guidelines: Create, update and oversee the tech guidelines for all assets during production 

- Workflow/Pipeline Improvements: Define the content creation pipeline to maximize performance, quality and efficiency 

- Assisting tool development: Collaborate with tech artist and progs to improve our internal tools.

- Documentation: Create, maintain and promote internal documentation to support onboarding and technical references 

- Create Templates: Create templates in Photoshop, Substance, and 3DS Max for standardization (everyone works with the same specification and avoid discrepancies), efficiency in production (avoid manual repetitive work and save time), Technical Compliance (include essential technical overlays such as UV maps, mem budgets, etc.) and Quality control. 

- Assets Integration: Integrate work files and assets provided by the internal team (ex. Substance Painter and 3DS Max files) into Anvil. Ensure the assets are hooked up for in-game but also for other departments (Rigging, VFX, etc.) 

- Proactive bug fixing: Anticipate, identify and resolve issues related to assets 

- Assist the team in any technical issue related with the art pipeline 

- Become the Go-To person for engine art related topics

Qualifications
- Strong knowledge of art related software, such as Photoshop, 3DsMax, Blender, Substance package. 

- Experience with commercial game engines, such as Unity or Unreal 

- C# Scripting Skills. XAML or tool development experience is a plus. 

- Self-organized, used to work with Jira, Trello or similar. 

- Proactive and problem solver. 

- Excellent interpersonal skills and great verbal and written communication skills in English 

- Nice to have previous experience working in a Studio or within videogames projects.

Additional Information
Benefits: 
 
- Private Health Insurance and fitness subsidies.

- Employee mental health assistance.

- Tickets restaurant

- Free coffee, fruits and daily breakfast.

- Spectacular roof-top terrace with sea views

Ubisoft is a global leader in gaming with teams across the world creating original and memorable gaming experiences, from Assassin’s Creed, Rainbow Six to Just Dance and more. We believe diverse perspectives help both players and teams thrive. If you’re passionate about innovation and pushing entertainment boundaries, join our journey and help create the unknown!

job.description:
Job Description
Sous la responsabilité du Lead Engine Programmer, vous interviendrez sur le développement, l'amélioration et l'optimisation du système qui permet de gérer la physique du jeu. Pour cela voici vos missions: 
 
- Maintenance et debugging du système physique (investigation, correction de bugs)

- Analyse et résolution de problématiques techniques (collisions, particules...etc)

- Développement de nouvelles features (simulation physique, placement et orientation d’objets)

- Optimisation des performances (collisions, physique temps réel)

Qualifications
- Vous possédez une expérience significative en développement C++ dans notre industrie, 

- Vous avez une bonne maîtrise d'un moteur physique comme Havok, Chaos, Bullet ou PhysX que vous avez pu utiliser dans une production de jeu,

- Vous êtes autonome, agissez de manière proactive et vous avez un bon sens du relationnel, 

- Votre niveau d‘anglais vous permet d’échanger facilement dans un contexte international,

Additional Information
Nous rejoindre c’est avoir accès dès le premier jour à : 
 
- Notre plateforme interne de e-learning pour enfin vous former sur les outils dont vous aviez tant besoin ; 

- Notre ludothèque où vous pourrez emprunter les derniers jeux Ubisoft, ceux de la concurrence, consoles et jeux de sociétés ; 

- Notre CSE et ses tarifs préférentiels sur une large gamme de spectacles, salles de cinéma, concerts, salles de sport, parcs d’attractions, et pleins d’autres bons plans. 

 Et après 1 an ?

Error handling and retry strategies

 Windows and/or Linux

 LoopMe is an AI company solving one of advertising’s hardest problems: making brand advertising actually measurable — and making it perform. Our platform runs patented machine learning models across billions of consumer signals in real time, optimising campaigns toward outcomes like purchase intent, brand lift, and foot traffic rather than proxy metrics like clicks.  We operate a high-load programmatic infrastructure — processing millions of ad requests per second with sub-200ms response times globally. This isn’t a layer on top of someone else’s stack; it’s built from the ground up, in-house, by the team you’d be joining.  The opportunity
 You’ll own the entire Unity product surface at LoopMe — the SDK layer that bridges our native iOS and Android products into the Unity ecosystem for game and app developers. You’ll have full architectural autonomy over how our Unity packages are designed, tested, and shipped, working closely with our iOS, Android, and QE teams to keep native and Unity experiences in lockstep. This role reports to the VP Engineering, SDK
 What you’ll do

- Own and operate the entire Unity product surface, with full architectural autonomy and per-platform customisation.

- Build and manage open source publishing for LoopMe ’s Unity packages, applying licensing best practices.

- Establish and run CI/CD pipelines for the Unity product surface.

- Drive parity between native iOS and Android platforms through proactive cross-team collaboration.

- Build generic, reusable tooling that Unity packages across the SDK portfolio can share.

- Develop and maintain LoopMe ’s Unity validator app.

- Manage Unity license administration across the SDK organisation.

- Partner with QE on cross-platform testing and support integration partners with clear SDK documentation.

 What you’ll bring
 Essential:

- Experience across cross-platform mobile and SDK development — iOS, Android, and Unity — including dependency resolution and wrapping native code and binaries inside Unity.

- Strong architectural background in modular Unity SDK design: dependency injection, bridging native iOS/Android SDKs into Unity through C/C++, and building Unity Editor tooling.

- Proficiency in C#, Kotlin, Swift, and Objective-C++.

- A track record publishing and maintaining open source software, with working knowledge of licensing and distribution through NPM, NuGet, and Unity Package Manager.

- Working knowledge of privacy and consent frameworks used in ad tech — GDPR, CCPA, TCF, GPP, COPPA, CMPs, and App Tracking Transparency.

 Nice to have:

- Familiarity with ad tech industry practices and client-server architecture patterns.

- Experience with CI/CD and build tooling such as GitHub Actions, Fastlane, Gradle, or Bazel.

- Comfort using agentic coding assistants, such as Claude Code, as part of a development workflow.

- Experience with mobile test automation tools such as Maestro, BrowserStack, or TestRail.

 The Role
 We are seeking an Interactive Technology Developer with strong Unity and C# experience to help create interactive experiences for trade shows, events, museums, and branded environments.
 This role is ideal for a developer who enjoys solving technical challenges, integrating emerging technologies, and bringing physical and digital systems together to create memorable experiences.
 Projects frequently involve Unity applications communicating with external systems, integrating third-party hardware, deploying emerging technologies, and supporting installations in real-world environments. While Unity and C# development will be the primary focus, this role emphasizes technical integration and systems development.
 The successful candidate will work closely with senior developers, designers, producers, and AV specialists to bring unique experiences to life.
 No two projects are exactly alike. You may find yourself putting the finishing touches on a custom game scene, integrating a computer vision framework into Unity, developing communication between applications using OSC, connecting to a badge registration platform through an API, or testing applications prior to deployment.
 We are looking for someone who is curious, adaptable, technically versatile, and excited to learn new technologies as project needs evolve.
 Location: Remote (Milwaukee, WI area preferred for occasional in-office collaboration)
 What You'll Do

- Develop and maintain interactive applications using Unity and C#.

- Integrate third-party SDKs, APIs, and external hardware into Unity applications.

- Integrate cameras, sensors, tracking systems, and other interactive technologies into live experiences.

- Build communication workflows between applications, devices, and external systems using technologies such as DMX, OSC, WebSockets, TCP/UDP, HTTP APIs, and related protocols.

- Integrate cloud services, internal business systems, registration platforms, and third-party event technologies into interactive experiences.

- Evaluate, prototype, and deploy emerging technologies including AI, computer vision, motion tracking, and interactive hardware platforms.

- Research and evaluate new software platforms, frameworks, and technologies for future projects.

- Assist with hardware selection, system setup, deployment, and technical documentation.

- Create technical diagrams, deployment plans, and installation documentation.

- Perform software QA, testing, optimization, and troubleshooting across software and hardware systems.

- Support deployed experiences during installation, testing, and live events as needed.

 What We're Looking For

- Strong proficiency in C# and object-oriented programming principles.

- Professional experience developing applications in Unity.

- Experience integrating third-party SDKs, APIs, middleware, or external hardware into applications.

- Familiarity with networking and communication protocols such as OSC, TCP/IP, UDP, WebSockets, REST APIs, or similar technologies.

- Experience working with sensors, cameras, tracking systems, or other interactive hardware is strongly preferred.

- Demonstrated ability to learn and apply new technologies, frameworks, and APIs independently.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to diagnose and resolve technical issues across multiple interconnected systems.

- Familiarity with technologies such as computer vision, AI services, machine learning frameworks, or real-time media systems is a plus.

- Basic familiarity with web technologies such as JavaScript, HTML, and REST-based services for integration purposes.

- Experience working in collaborative development environments and managing multiple priorities simultaneously.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.

 Bonus Experience
 Experience with any of the following is a plus:

- Computer vision frameworks (MediaPipe, OpenCV, etc.)

- Depth cameras and tracking systems (ZED, Azure Kinect, Intel RealSense, etc.)

- AI service integrations

- Interactive exhibit, museum, trade show, or experiential technology projects

- V systems and show control technologies

- TouchDesigner, or other real-time platforms

- Linux, scripting, or server administration

- Cloud platforms and deployment workflows

 Why Stamm Media 

- Work with a collaborative, high-performing team that genuinely enjoys working together.

- Build experiences using emerging technologies including AI, computer vision, interactive systems, and experiential technology platforms.

- Collaborate on innovative, high-impact projects for major brands.

- Help create immersive experiences seen by audiences nationwide.

- Be part of a respected event technology company with a national footprint.

- Work on projects where creativity, experimentation, and technical innovation are encouraged.

 If you enjoy combining software, hardware, and emerging technologies to create unforgettable experiences, we'd love to hear from you.

job.description:
The Problem
 Young people are more connected online than ever, yet lonelier than any generation before them.
 Most digital platforms are designed for passive consumption on screens, pulling people away from the environments they live in.
 We are exploring the opposite:
 technology that brings people together in real-world environments. 
 To do that, software must understand place , not just users and clicks.
 What We Are Building
 Vyry builds context-aware AI quests that get students to meet IRL. 
 The system turns environments — starting with university campuses — into interactive canvases where students coordinate actions and co-create digital artifacts anchored to real locations.
 We are in closed beta and measure strong signals:

- 12k → 175k students reached in 2025

- 25% of MAUs complete quests

- pilots show up to 40% reduction in social isolation 

 The team combines consumer product, spatial, and game-world expertise , with former talents from: Roblox • Niantic • Ubisoft alongside a research layer that includes: 2 professors + 4 PhDs 
 The company is also part of:
 Google AI Startup Program and prototyping on Meta’s invite-only Wearables SDK 
 What You Would Work On
 Core product stack includes:

- Unity real-time spatial environment layer

- persistent digital artifacts anchored to real-world locations

- multi-user spatial interaction systems

- AI-assisted pipelines for generating spatial objects

 Hard Problems We’re Exploring

- Persistent spatial worlds — artifacts anchored to real places that persist across users, sessions, and devices

- Multi-user spatial synchronization — ensuring multiple users see and interact with the same artifact in the same physical location

- Mobile-first spatial computing — running tracking, rendering, anchors, and networking within phone and wearable hardware constraints

- Real-time spatial rendering with AI context — Unity rendering environments in real time while receiving contextual input from large world models and action models

 Role
 We are looking for a senior Unity engineer who wants to become a founding technical contributor .
 You would help:

- shape Unity architecture

- design spatial persistence systems

- build multi-user spatial interaction systems

- integrate AI-assisted development workflows

- define the long-term technical direction of the platform

 We are not looking for someone to simply use Unity.
We are looking for someone who wants to help define the architecture of a new spatial computing product category. 
 Compensation
 This is an equity-first founding role.
 Compensation is equity-only until our next funding round (target H2 2026). 
 You can join either:

- Part-time , while keeping your current role

- Full-time

 Many experienced engineers start part-time first while evaluating the opportunity.
 This role is designed for someone who wants to build a startup without having to start one alone from scratch .
 Who This Is For
 Engineers who:

- have deep Unity experience (typically 8–10+ years) 

- have shipped complex real-time systems

- enjoy architecting systems rather than just implementing features 

- are curious about AI integration into interactive environments 

 This often resonates with engineers who have spent years inside larger companies and want to build something meaningful with ownership .
 Who This Is NOT For
 Please do not apply if:

- you are looking for a salaried job today 

- you want a freelance contract or short-term gig 

- you are bridging time until your next role 

 This is a founding role with startup emotions .
 If Interested
 Send:

- GitHub or portfolio

- examples of Unity systems you built

- anything you’ve experimented with involving AI

 Please also include short answers to the questions below.
 PS: If you have spent years building complex Unity systems and occasionally think:
 “If I were part of a startup, I would architect it differently.” 
 You are probably the person we are hoping reads this.

job.description:
Help us ship new 3D immersive events and content to the VRChat community, reliably, efficiently, and with a high quality bar.

 Join the VRChat team!

 We’re building the future of immersive, user-generated worlds, where anyone, anywhere, can connect, play, explore, and express themselves.

 We’re looking for a Unity Technical Artist to support VRChat ’s live ops events and content pipeline. This role sits at the intersection of art and engineering: you’ll be hands-on in Unity, you’ll write scripts/tools to make publishing more efficient, and you’ll help our events and content ship smoothly across platforms.

 You’ll partner closely with artists, designers, and engineers, so creative work moves from “done” to “shipped” without surprises.

 What You'll Do

- Own and evolve the end-to-end Unity content pipeline for live ops assets, helping us ship 3D props and content updates with consistency and speed.

- Implement and validate 3D assets in Unity: prefabs, materials, shaders, collisions, LODs, lighting setups, and import settings, with an eye toward performance and reliability.

- Build and maintain tools, scripts, and automation (primarily in C# and Udon) that reduce manual work, prevent common errors, and make publishing repeatable.

- Create lightweight quality gates for content: asset validation checks, naming/structure conventions, performance budgets, and “ready to ship” checklists.

- Debug content and pipeline issues across disciplines, working with engineers on technical constraints and with artists on asset readiness.

- Collaborate with Product Design and Creators partners to ensure content supports the intended user experience and meets our quality bar.

- Document workflows so the whole team can move faster as we scale content volume in 2026.

 Who You Are

- You have 3+ years experience as a Technical Artist, Tools Artist, or similar role (or equivalent shipped work).

- You’re deeply comfortable in Unity and understand what it takes to ship real-time 3D content that performs well.

- You can write scripts (most likely C# ) and you’ve built tools or automation that helped teams move faster or reduced production risk.

- You understand 3D fundamentals (meshes, materials, textures, lighting, optimization) and can collaborate effectively with artists on asset quality.

- You think in systems and pipelines: you notice recurring failure modes, then design guardrails that prevent them.

- You communicate clearly across disciplines and enjoy being the person who turns ambiguity into a reliable workflow.

- You have a strong ownership mindset: you care about shipping, not just “building a perfect tool someday.”

 Bonus Points (Not required, but we’d be excited if you bring any of the following!)

- Experience building editor tooling, import automation, or asset validation pipelines in Unity.

- Familiarity with the VRChat creator toolchain: Unity + VRChat SDK (Worlds/Avatars) + Creator Companion (VCC/VPM)

- Experience building interactivity in VRChat worlds using Udon / UdonSharp (C# that compiles to Udon)

- Familiarity with common VRChat avatar components like PhysBones/Contacts and performance best practices.

- Experience optimizing content for multiple hardware tiers and platforms (PC + mobile constraints, etc.).

- Experience supporting live ops or high-cadence content publishing.

 Not sure if you meet every single requirement?
 We’d still love to hear from you. We know technical artists come from all kinds of backgrounds. If you’re excited to help ship a steady stream of 3D content to a global community, and you like making pipelines fast, safe, and human-friendly, please apply.
 Where You’ll Be
 This is a remote-first role. Work from wherever you do your best thinking. We’re a fully distributed company with team members across the globe. While we work asynchronously, overlap with U.S. time zones is needed for team collaboration.
 Benefits

- 100% Remote – work from anywhere in the world

- Health benefits for U.S. and Canadian employees

- 401K (U.S.) and RRSP (Canada) retirement plans

- Stock options

- Unlimited/flexible vacation policy

- Paid parental leave

- Generous holiday schedule

 VRChat is an equal-opportunity employer, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. VRChat fosters a diverse, creative, and collaborative environment where anyone can contribute to any of the ongoing projects or direction of the roadmap at any time. If you’re a passionate team player who wants to have an impact on a dynamic team, we’d love to hear from you! 

 All job offers are subject to early stage ID checks, satisfactory referencing and background checks.

job.description:
Who We Are

 At YallaPlay , We are a rapidly growing startup mobile gaming studio on a mission to bring people together through play, we create exciting mobile games that bring joy to millions of players worldwide. Founded in Austin, Texas, we’ve since expanded to Brazil and the UAE, growing our diverse and talented team of creators. We pride ourselves on a fun and collaborative work environment, with a remote-friendly culture and a dedication to producing high-quality, engaging games. Our current titles, including “Spades Masters” (iOS/Android), have been enjoyed by millions of players globally. 

 Our passion lies in reinventing card games infusing them with fresh mechanics, beautiful design, and social features that spark connection and excitement. As we continue to scale, we’re looking for creative, driven individuals who are excited to help shape the future of multiplayer mobile gaming in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.

 Join us and be part of building something big from the ground up.

 The Opportunity

 We're looking for a Unity Developer to help build high-quality mobile games faster and smarter. Reporting to the Lead Unity Developer, you'll use modern AI development tools alongside your technical expertise to implement game features, prototype ideas rapidly, solve complex engineering problems, and continuously improve development velocity.

 This role spans the entire game development lifecycle, from rapid prototyping to live operations. Success requires strong Unity fundamentals, excellent engineering judgment, and the ability to use AI as a force multiplier while maintaining high standards for code quality, performance, and player experience.

 This position is remote and from Brazil.

 What You’ll Be Doing

- Develop and implement mobile games in Unity for iOS and Android.

- Use AI-powered development tools to accelerate coding, debugging, refactoring, documentation, testing, and prototyping while maintaining production-quality standards.

- Collaborate with designers, producers, artists, backend engineers, and QA to deliver polished player experiences.

- Write clean, scalable, maintainable C# code and validate AI-generated code before production use.

- Rapidly prototype gameplay mechanics and iterate based on team feedback.

- Optimize performance across a wide range of mobile devices using Unity profiling tools.

- Debug complex gameplay, networking, memory, and platform-specific issues.

- Implement gameplay systems, UI, animations, VFX, audio, and live operations features.

- Contribute to CI/CD, build automation, and deployment pipelines.

- Review code, improve engineering standards, and contribute to reusable systems and internal tools.

- Continuously evaluate new AI tools and workflows that improve team productivity.

- Participate in Agile development processes, including sprint planning and daily standups.

 What We’re Looking For

 What you need to have:

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Interactive Media, or equivalent experience.

- 
 5+ years developing mobile games with Unity.

- At least 2 shipped mobile game titles.

- Excellent C# programming skills.

- Strong understanding of Unity architecture, UI Toolkit/uGUI, prefabs, asset management, animation, audio, and scene management.

- Experience building both 2D and 3D mobile games.

- Experience optimizing CPU, GPU, memory, and battery performance.

- Experience with REST APIs, WebSockets, or multiplayer networking.

- Strong debugging and problem-solving skills.

- Experience working in Agile teams.

- Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

 AI-First Development

 We expect our engineers to use AI as part of their daily workflow. You should:

- Be comfortable using AI coding assistants (such as Unity AI, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, ChatGPT, or similar).

- Know how to write effective prompts for technical tasks.

- Critically review, validate, test, and improve AI-generated code rather than accepting it blindly.

- Use AI to accelerate debugging, documentation, testing, refactoring, and code generation.

- Continuously experiment with new AI workflows that improve development speed without compromising quality.

- Understand the limitations, risks, and security considerations of AI-assisted software development.

 Why YallaPlay 

 What You Get

- 
 Real Impact – You’ll work on meaningful projects that reach a global audience.

- 
 Collaborative Culture – Small team, big ambition. We keep things fun, respectful, and feedback-driven.

 Benefits & Perks

- Competitive salary

- Remote-first and flexible schedule- Digital nomad friendly

- Generous paid time off

- Paid birthdays off

- Growth opportunities and access to learning resources

- A team that actually loves games—and each other

 Next Steps

 Ready to join the team? We’d love to hear from you!

- Apply 

- Share sample code and projects (GitHub)

 We review every application carefully and will be in touch if there’s a fit. Good luck!
